decisions.reason: A classic lever handle fits squarely in the firm's core hardware range, needed little specific investment to launch, and one year is too short to judge its results, so management keeps it.
A handle family needs tooling for several variants and dealer catalogue listings, and those sunk costs plus the firm's stated commitment favour persisting with it.
Any weak early uptake of a new handle design can still be blamed on slow adoption by architects and the trade, so the product stays.
Design handles take time to be specified into building projects, and the tooling has already been paid for, so management continues the product.
As a full lever handle family with substantial tooling and catalogue presence, it carries strong commitment and justification pressure to keep it.

The L700 electronic access system was publicly launched with a claimed market-unique light technology and points toward the firm's digital direction, so the large R&D investment and public commitment make dropping it very unlikely.
